data.content_ref: inline:The target's 'pragmatic wager' defense fails because it implicitly relies on the Principle of Uniformity (that the future will resemble the past) to assign any rational weight to past survival. Popper explicitly rejects induction precisely because past success logically entails nothing about future performance; by arguing that a theory surviving severe tests is the 'only rational choice' due to its demonstrated 'fitness,' the target smuggles in the very inductive assumption it claims to avoid. If the future need not resemble the past, a theory's past 'fitness' offers no pragmatic advantage over a falsified one or a random guess, rendering the preference indefensible on Popper's own strict terms without contradicting his core rejection of induction.
